   198	The purpose of this project is to explore some techniques in supervised learning.
   199	 
   200	 * Decision Trees
   201	     * For the decision tree, you should implement or steal a decision tree algorithm. Be sure to use some form of pruning. You are not required to use information gain (for example, there is something called the GINI index that is sometimes used) to split attributes, but you should describe whatever it is that you do use.
   202	 * k-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN)
   203	     * You should implement kNN. Use different values of k.  
   204	 * Boosted Trees
   205	     * Implement a boosted version of your decision trees. As before, you will want to use some form of pruning, but presumably because you're using boosting you can afford to be much more aggressive about your pruning.
   206	 * Support Vector Machines (SVM)
   207	     * You should implement (for sufficiently loose definitions of implement including "download") SVMs. This should be done in such a way that you can swap out kernel functions. I'd like to see at least two.

    92	def heatmap(data, row_labels, col_labels, ax=None, cbar_kw={}, cbarlabel="", **kwargs):

    94	    Create a heatmap from a numpy array and two lists of labels.

    96	    Parameters

   114	
   115	    if not ax:

   139	    plt.title('epsilon')

   142	    # Turn spines off and create white grid.

   144	        spine.set_visible(False)
   145	
   146	    ax.set_xticks(np.arange(data.shape[1] + 1) - .5, minor=True)

   148	    ax.grid(which="minor", color="w", linestyle='-', linewidth=3)

   154	def annotate_heatmap(im, data=None, valfmt="{x:.2f}", textcolors=["black", "white"], threshold=None, **textkw):
   155	    """
   156	    A function to annotate a heatmap.
   157	
   158	    Parameters
   159	    ----------
   160	    im
   161	        The AxesImage to be labeled.
   162	    data
   163	        Data used to annotate.  If None, the image's data is used.  Optional.
   164	    valfmt
   165	        The format of the annotations inside the heatmap.  This should either
   166	        use the string format method, e.g. "$ {x:.2f}", or be a
   167	        `matplotlib.ticker.Formatter`.  Optional.
   168	    textcolors
   169	        A list or array of two color specifications.  The first is used for
   170	        values below a threshold, the second for those above.  Optional.
   171	    threshold
   172	        Value in data units according to which the colors from textcolors are
   173	        applied.  If None (the default) uses the middle of the colormap as
   174	        separation.  Optional.
   175	    **kwargs
   176	        All other arguments are forwarded to each call to `text` used to create
   177	        the text labels.
   178	    """
   179	
   180	    if not isinstance(data, (list, np.ndarray)):
   181	        data = im.get_array()
   182	
   183	    # Normalize the threshold to the images color range.
   184	    if threshold is not None:
   185	        threshold = im.norm(threshold)
   186	    else:
   187	        threshold = im.norm(data.max()) / 2.
   188	
   189	    # Set default alignment to center, but allow it to be
   190	    # overwritten by textkw.
   191	    kw = dict(horizontalalignment="center",
   192	              verticalalignment="center")
   193	    kw.update(textkw)
   194	
   195	    # Get the formatter in case a string is supplied
   196	    if isinstance(valfmt, str):
   197	        valfmt = matplotlib.ticker.StrMethodFormatter(valfmt)
   198	
   199	    # Loop over the data and create a `Text` for each "pixel".
   200	    # Change the text's color depending on the data.
   201	    texts = []
   202	    for i in range(data.shape[0]):
   203	        for j in range(data.shape[1]):
   204	            kw.update(color=textcolors[int(im.norm(data[i, j]) > threshold)])
   205	            text = im.axes.text(j, i, valfmt(data[i, j], None), **kw)
   206	            texts.append(text)
   207	
   208	    return texts

   211	# Citation: https://learning.oreilly.com/library/view/reinforcement-learning-algorithms/9781789131116/ab06aa68-01f9-481e-94ac-4c6748c3b858.xhtml
   212	def eval_state_action(env, V, s, a, gamma=0.99):
   213	    return np.sum([p * ((rew - 0.01 * _) + gamma * V[next_s]) for p, next_s, rew, _ in env.P[s][a]])

   216	def policy_evaluation(env, V, policy, nS, epsilon=0.0001, gamma=0.99):
   217	    while True:
   218	        delta = 0
   219	        for s in range(nS):
   220	            old_v = V[s]
   221	            V[s] = eval_state_action(env, V, s, policy[s], gamma)
   222	            delta = max(delta, np.abs(old_v - V[s]))
   223	        if delta < epsilon:
   224	            break
   225	
   226	
   227	def policy_improvement(env, V, policy, nA, nS, gamma=0.99):
   228	    policy_stable = True
   229	    for s in range(nS):
   230	        old_a = policy[s]
   231	        policy[s] = np.argmax([eval_state_action(env, V, s, a, gamma) for a in range(nA)])
   232	        if old_a != policy[s]:
   233	            policy_stable = False
   234	    return policy_stable

   237	def run_pi_episodes(env, V, policy, num_games=100):
   238	    tot_rew = 0
   239	    state = env.reset()
   240	    for _ in range(num_games):
   241	        done = False
   242	        tot_run = 0
   243	        while not done:
   244	            next_state, reward, done, _ = env.step(policy[state])
   245	            state = next_state
   246	            tot_rew += reward
   247	            tot_run += 1
   248	            if done or tot_run > 1000:
   249	                done = True
   250	                state = env.reset()
   251	    return float(tot_rew / num_games)

   553	def value_iteration(env, nA, nS, epsilon=0.0001, gamma=0.99):
   554	    V = np.zeros(nS)
   555	    it = 0
   556	    delta_vals = []
   557	    avg_V = []
   558	    while True:
   559	        delta = 0
   560	        # update the value for each state
   561	        for s in range(nS):
   562	            old_v = V[s]
   563	            V[s] = np.max([eval_state_action(env, V, s, a, gamma) for a in range(nA)])  # equation 3.10
   564	            delta = max(delta, np.abs(old_v - V[s]))
   565	        # if stable, break the cycle
   566	        delta_vals.append(delta)
   567	        avg_V.append(np.mean(V))
   568	        if delta < epsilon:
   569	            break
   570	        # else:
   571	        #    print('Iter:', it, ' delta:', np.round(delta, 5))
   572	        it += 1
   573	    return V, delta_vals, it, avg_V

   579	    max_run = 0

   585	            # choose the best action using the value function
   586	            action = np.argmax([eval_state_action(env, V, state, a, gamma) for a in range(nA)])  # (11)
   587	            next_state, reward, done, _ = env.step(action)
   588	            state = next_state
   589	            tot_rew += reward
   590	            max_run += 1
   591	            if done:
   592	                state = env.reset()
   593	            if max_run > 10000:
   594	                state = env.reset()
   595	                done = True
   596	                tot_rew += 0
   597	                max_run = 0
   598	
   599	    # print('Won %i of %i games!' % (tot_rew, num_games))
   600	    return float(tot_rew / num_games)

  1261	def eps_greedy(Q, s, eps=0.1):
  1262	    '''
  1263	    Epsilon greedy policy
  1264	    '''
  1265	    if np.random.uniform(0, 1) < eps:
  1266	        # Choose a random action
  1267	        return np.random.randint(Q.shape[1])
  1268	    else:
  1269	        # Choose the action of a greedy policy
  1270	        return greedy(Q, s)

  1273	def greedy(Q, s):
  1274	    '''
  1275	    Greedy policy
  1276	    return the index corresponding to the maximum action-state value
  1277	    '''
  1278	    return np.argmax(Q[s])

  1281	def run_episodes(env, Q, num_episodes=100):
  1282	    '''
  1283	    Run some episodes to test the policy
  1284	    '''
  1285	    tot_rew = []

  1289	        done = False
  1290	        game_rew = 0
  1291	
  1292	        while not done:
  1293	            # select a greedy action
  1294	            next_state, rew, done, _ = env.step(greedy(Q, state))
  1295	
  1296	            state = next_state
  1297	            game_rew += rew
  1298	            if done:
  1299	                state = env.reset()
  1300	                tot_rew.append(game_rew)
  1301	
  1302	    return np.mean(tot_rew)

  1305	def Q_learning(env, lr=0.01, lr_min=0.0001, lr_decay=0.99, num_episodes=10000, eps=0.3, gamma=0.95, eps_decay=0.00005,
  1306	               eps_min=0.0001):
  1307	    nA = env.action_space.n
  1308	    nS = env.observation_space.n
  1309	
  1310	    # Initialize the Q matrix
  1311	    # Q: matrix nS*nA where each row represent a state and each colums represent a different action
  1312	    Q = np.zeros((nS, nA))
  1313	    games_reward = []
  1314	    test_rewards = []
  1315	
  1316	    for ep in range(num_episodes):
  1317	        state = env.reset()
  1318	        done = False
  1319	        tot_rew = 0
  1320	
  1321	        # decay the epsilon value until it reaches the threshold of 0.01
  1322	        if eps > eps_min:
  1323	            eps *= eps_decay
  1324	            eps = max(eps, eps_min)
  1325	
  1326	        # decay the learning rate until it reaches the threshold of lr_min
  1327	        if lr > lr_min:
  1328	            lr *= lr_decay
  1329	            lr = max(lr, lr_min)
  1330	
  1331	        # loop the main body until the environment stops
  1332	        while not done:
  1333	            # select an action following the eps-greedy policy
  1334	            action = eps_greedy(Q, state, eps)
  1335	
  1336	            next_state, rew, done, _ = env.step(action)  # Take one step in the environment
  1337	            rew -= (0.01 * done)
  1338	
  1339	            # Q-learning update the state-action value (get the max Q value for the next state)
  1340	            Q[state][action] = Q[state][action] + lr * (rew + gamma * np.max(Q[next_state]) - Q[state][action])
  1341	
  1342	            state = next_state
  1343	            tot_rew += rew
  1344	            if done:
  1345	                games_reward.append(tot_rew)
  1346	
  1347	    return Q

   149	## CS 7641 Assignment 3: Unsupervised Learning and Dimensionality Reduction 
   150	The purpose of this project is to explore some techniques in unsupervised learning.
   151	 
   152	#### Clustering
   153	
   154	* k-means clustering
   155	* Expectation Maximization
   156	
   157	Each clustering algorithm will be run on two datasets and compared and contrasted, using measures which have no knowledge of the ground truth (i.e. the labels) the BIC Scores, Inertia Curve, Davies-Bouldin Index, Calinski-Harabasz Index, and Silohuette scores, but then also contrasting to ground truth scores of V-Measure, Adjusted Rand Index, and Adjusted Mutual Information Index.
   158	
   159	#### Dimensionality Reduction
   160	
   161	Each DR algorithm will be run on the same datasets as clustering and by reviewing a specific metric per algorithm it will be possible to determine the optimal number of clusters.
   162	
   163	* PCA
   164	   * Explained Variance Ratio
   165	* ICA
   166	  * Average Kurtosis
   167	* Randomized Projections
   168	  * Mean Reconstruction Error
   169	* Locally Linear Embedding
   170	  * Mean Reconstruction Error
   171	   
   172	After running the clustering and DR algorithms independently, the same clustering metrics and algorithms will be run on the datasets after applying the optimal number of dimensionality reduction.

   174	Finally, one dataset is chosen to run the neural network from A1, first replacing the data with the dimension reduced data and finding the Train/Test ROC, then determining the ideal clusters and appending them to the data and running the neural network classification.

# Citation: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/auto_examples/cluster/plot_kmeans_digits.html#sphx-glr-auto-examples-cluster-plot-kmeans-digits-py
def bench_k_means(estimator, labels, name, data, sample_size, n_clusters, random_state, filename, verbose=False):
    t0 = time()
    estimator.fit(data)
    fit_time = time() - t0

    homo = metrics.homogeneity_score(labels, estimator.predict(data))
    comp = metrics.completeness_score(labels, estimator.predict(data))
    v_meas = metrics.v_measure_score(labels, estimator.predict(data))
    ari = metrics.adjusted_rand_score(labels, estimator.predict(data))
    ami = metrics.adjusted_mutual_info_score(labels, estimator.predict(data))
    fks = metrics.fowlkes_mallows_score(labels, estimator.predict(data))
    silo = metrics.silhouette_score(data, estimator.predict(data), metric='euclidean', sample_size=sample_size,
                                    random_state=random_state)
    dbs = metrics.davies_bouldin_score(data, estimator.predict(data))
    chs = metrics.calinski_harabasz_score(data, estimator.predict(data))
    iner = estimator.inertia_
    if verbose:
        print('%-9s\t%d\t%.2fs\t%.2f\t%.3f\t%.3f\t%.3f\t%.3f\t%.3f\t%.3f\t%.3f\t%i\t%i'
              % (name, n_clusters, (time() - t0), homo, comp, v_meas, ari, ami, fks, silo, dbs, chs, iner)
              )

    return fit_time, homo, comp, v_meas, ari, ami, fks, silo, dbs, chs, iner


# Citation: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/auto_examples/cluster/plot_kmeans_silhouette_analysis.html#sphx-glr-auto-examples-cluster-plot-kmeans-silhouette-analysis-py
def silo_analysis(X, y, clusterer, n_clusters, random_state, filename):
    if filename == "Chess":
        col1, col2 = 0, 5
    else:
        col1, col2 = 13, 11

    cluster_labels = clusterer.fit_predict(X)

    # The silhouette_score gives the average value for all the samples.
    # This gives a perspective into the density and separation of the formed
    # clusters
    silhouette_avg = silhouette_score(X, cluster_labels, metric='euclidean', sample_size=400, random_state=random_state)

    plt.figure()

    # The 1st subplot is the silhouette plot
    # The silhouette coefficient can range from -1, 1 but in this example all
    # lie within [-0.1, 1]
    plt.xlim([-0.1, 1])
    # The (n_clusters+1)*10 is for inserting blank space between silhouette
    # plots of individual clusters, to demarcate them clearly.
    plt.ylim([0, len(X) + (n_clusters + 1) * 10])

    # Compute the silhouette scores for each sample
    sample_silhouette_values = silhouette_samples(X, cluster_labels)

    y_lower = 10
    for i in range(n_clusters):
        # Aggregate the silhouette scores for samples belonging to
        # cluster i, and sort them
        ith_cluster_silhouette_values = \
            sample_silhouette_values[cluster_labels == i]

        ith_cluster_silhouette_values.sort()

        size_cluster_i = ith_cluster_silhouette_values.shape[0]
        y_upper = y_lower + size_cluster_i

        cmap = cm.get_cmap("tab10")
        color = cmap(float(i) / n_clusters)
        plt.fill_betweenx(np.arange(y_lower, y_upper),
                          0, ith_cluster_silhouette_values,
                          facecolor=color, edgecolor=color, alpha=0.7)

        # Label the silhouette plots with their cluster numbers at the middle
        plt.text(-0.05, y_lower + 0.5 * size_cluster_i, str(i))

        # Compute the new y_lower for next plot
        y_lower = y_upper + 10  # 10 for the 0 samples

    plt.title("The silhouette plot for the various %d KMeans clusters." % n_clusters)

    plt.xlabel("The silhouette coefficient values")
    plt.ylabel("Cluster label")

    # The vertical line for average silhouette score of all the values
    plt.axvline(x=silhouette_avg, color="red", linestyle="--")

    plt.yticks([])  # Clear the yaxis labels / ticks
    plt.xticks([-0.1, 0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1])

    plt.savefig("Images\\" + filename + "Silhouette Plot for " + str(n_clusters) + " clusters")
    plt.show()

    # 2nd Plot showing the actual clusters formed
    plt.figure()

    cmap = cm.get_cmap("tab10")
    colors = cmap(cluster_labels.astype(float) / n_clusters)

    plt.scatter(X.iloc[:, col1], X.iloc[:, col2], marker='.', s=30, lw=0, alpha=0.7,
                c=colors, edgecolor='k')

    # Labeling the clusters
    centers = clusterer.cluster_centers_
    # Draw white circles at cluster centers
    plt.scatter(centers[:, col1], centers[:, col2], marker='o',
                c="white", alpha=1, s=200, edgecolor='k')

    for i, c in enumerate(centers):
        plt.scatter(c[col1], c[col2], marker='$%d$' % i, alpha=1,
                    s=50, edgecolor='k')

    plt.title("Visualization of the clustered data for %d KMeans clusters." % n_clusters)
    plt.xlabel("Feature space for the 1st feature")
    plt.ylabel("Feature space for the 2nd feature")
    plt.savefig("Images\\" + filename + "Visualization " + str(n_clusters) + " clusters")

    plt.show()


# Citation: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/auto_examples/cluster/plot_kmeans_stability_low_dim_dense.html#sphx-glr-auto-examples-cluster-plot-kmeans-stability-low-dim-dense-py
def init_analysis(X, y, n_clusters, filename):
    # Number of run (with randomly generated dataset) for each strategy so as
    # to be able to compute an estimate of the standard deviation
    n_runs = 5

    # k-means models can do several random inits so as to be able to trade
    # CPU time for convergence robustness
    n_init_range = np.array([1, 5, 10, 15, 20, 50, 75, 100])

    # Part 1: Quantitative evaluation of various init methods

    plt.figure()
    plots = []
    legends = []

    cases = [
        (KMeans, 'k-means++', {}),
        (KMeans, 'random', {}),
        (MiniBatchKMeans, 'k-means++', {'max_no_improvement': 3}),
        (MiniBatchKMeans, 'random', {'max_no_improvement': 3, 'init_size': 500}),
    ]

    for factory, init, params in cases:
        print("Evaluation of %s with %s init" % (factory.__name__, init))
        inertia = np.empty((len(n_init_range), n_runs))

        for run_id in range(n_runs):
            for i, n_init in enumerate(n_init_range):
                km = factory(n_clusters=n_clusters, init=init, random_state=run_id,
                             n_init=n_init, **params).fit(X)
                inertia[i, run_id] = km.inertia_
        p = plt.errorbar(n_init_range, inertia.mean(axis=1), inertia.std(axis=1))
        plots.append(p[0])
        legends.append("%s with %s init" % (factory.__name__, init))

    plt.xlabel('n_init')
    plt.ylabel('inertia')
    plt.legend(plots, legends)
    plt.title("Mean inertia for various k-means init across %d runs" % n_runs)
    plt.savefig(
            "Images\\" + filename + "Mean Interia across " + str(n_runs) + " runs and " + str(n_clusters) + " clusters")

def run_episodes(policy, S, R, p, num_episodes, num_resets):
    rew_arr = []
    for y in range(num_resets):
        forest_state = 0
        tot_rew = 0
        for x in range(num_episodes):
            forest_state = min(forest_state, S - 1)
            if np.random.rand(1) <= p:
                forest_state = -1
            else:
                tot_rew += R[forest_state][policy[forest_state]]
                if policy[forest_state] == 1:
                    forest_state = -1
            forest_state += 1
        rew_arr.append(tot_rew)
    return np.mean(rew_arr)

+    classifier.fit(X_train, y_train)
+    train_score = util.score_estimator(classifier, X_train, y_train)
+    test_score = util.score_estimator(classifier, X_test, y_test)
+
+    if make_graphs:
+        util.plot_learning_curve(
+            classifier,
+            algo,
+            file_stem,
+            X_train,
+            y_train,
+            ylim=(0.0, 1.05),
+            cv=min(numFolds, util._safe_cv_folds(y_train, numFolds)),
+            n_jobs=njobs,
+            debug=debug,
+        )
+
+        for parameter, values, options in [
+            ("max_depth", [1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 20, 50, 100, None], {"fString": True, "rotatex": True}),
+            ("min_samples_split", [2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 20], {}),
+            ("ccp_alpha", [0.0001, 0.001, 0.01, 0.1], {"log": True}),
+            ("criterion", ["gini", "entropy", "log_loss"], {"fString": True}),
+        ]:
+            base_params = dict(params)
+            base_params.pop(parameter, None)
+            test_class = DecisionTreeClassifier()
+            test_class.set_params(**base_params)
+            util.compute_vc(
+                algo,
+                parameter,
+                values,
+                X_train,
+                y_train,
+                X_test,
+                y_test,
+                classifier,
+                file_stem,
+                test_class,
+                base_params,
+                njobs=njobs,
+                debug=debug,
+                **options,
+            )
+
+    return time.time() - start, float(train_score), float(test_score)

from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import kurtosis
from sklearn.decomposition import FastICA, PCA
from sklearn.manifold import LocallyLinearEmbedding
from sklearn.metrics import mean_squared_error
from sklearn.random_projection import GaussianRandomProjection as GRP


BASE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
IMAGE_DIR = BASE_DIR / "Images"


def _ensure_image_dir():
    IMAGE_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return IMAGE_DIR


def _image_path(name):
    return _ensure_image_dir() / f"{name}.png"


def _as_array(X):
    return X.to_numpy() if hasattr(X, "to_numpy") else np.asarray(X)


def _component_range(X, upper=20, require_less_than_features=False, require_less_than_neighbors=None):
    data = _as_array(X)
    n_samples, n_features = data.shape
    max_components = min(upper, n_features, n_samples)
    if require_less_than_features:
        max_components = min(max_components, max(1, n_features - 1))
    if require_less_than_neighbors is not None:
        max_components = min(max_components, max(1, require_less_than_neighbors - 1))
    return list(range(1, max_components + 1))


def _plot_line(x_values, y_values, title, ylabel, filename, y_std=None):
    fig, ax = plt.subplots()
    ax.plot(x_values, y_values, marker="o")
    if y_std is not None:
        y_values = np.asarray(y_values)
        y_std = np.asarray(y_std)
        ax.fill_between(x_values, y_values - y_std, y_values + y_std, alpha=0.15)
    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=16)
    ax.set_xlabel("Number of Components", fontsize=14)
    ax.set_ylabel(ylabel, fontsize=14)
    ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(_image_path(filename))
    plt.close(fig)


def ulPCA(X, y, random_seed, filename, verbose=False):
    del y, verbose
    component_range = _component_range(X)
    if not component_range:
        return

    data = _as_array(X)
    explained = []
    cumulative = []
    reconstruction_error = []

    for n_components in component_range:
        pca = PCA(n_components=n_components, svd_solver="full", random_state=random_seed)
        transformed = pca.fit_transform(data)
        reconstructed = pca.inverse_transform(transformed)
        explained.append(float(np.sum(pca.explained_variance_ratio_)))
        cumulative.append(float(np.sum(pca.explained_variance_ratio_)))
        reconstruction_error.append(float(mean_squared_error(data, reconstructed)))

    _plot_line(
        component_range,
        cumulative,
        "PCA Cumulative Explained Variance",
        "Explained Variance Ratio",
        f"{filename} PCA Explained Variance",
    )
    _plot_line(
        component_range,
        reconstruction_error,
        "PCA Reconstruction Error",
        "Mean Squared Error",
        f"{filename} PCA Reconstruction Error",
    )


def ulICA(X, y, random_seed, filename, verbose=False):
    del y, verbose
    component_range = _component_range(X)
    if not component_range:
        return

    data = _as_array(X)
    avg_kurtosis = []
    reconstruction_error = []

    for n_components in component_range:
        ica = FastICA(n_components=n_components, random_state=random_seed, max_iter=1000, tol=0.001)
        transformed = ica.fit_transform(data)
        reconstructed = ica.inverse_transform(transformed)
        avg_kurtosis.append(float(np.mean(np.abs(kurtosis(transformed, axis=0, fisher=False, bias=False)))))
        reconstruction_error.append(float(mean_squared_error(data, reconstructed)))

    _plot_line(
        component_range,
        avg_kurtosis,
        "ICA Average Absolute Kurtosis",
        "Average |Kurtosis|",
        f"{filename} ICA Kurtosis",
    )
    _plot_line(
        component_range,
        reconstruction_error,
        "ICA Reconstruction Error",
        "Mean Squared Error",
        f"{filename} ICA Reconstruction Error",
    )


def randProj(X, y, random_seed, filename, verbose=False):
    del y, verbose
    component_range = _component_range(X)
    if not component_range:
        return

    data = _as_array(X)
    mean_errors = []
    std_errors = []

    for n_components in component_range:
        errors = []
        for seed in range(random_seed, random_seed + 5):
            rp = GRP(n_components=n_components, random_state=seed)
            transformed = rp.fit_transform(data)
            reconstructed = rp.inverse_transform(transformed)
            errors.append(float(mean_squared_error(data, reconstructed)))
        mean_errors.append(float(np.mean(errors)))
        std_errors.append(float(np.std(errors)))

    _plot_line(
        component_range,
        mean_errors,
        "Random Projection Reconstruction Error",
        "Mean Squared Error",
        f"{filename} RP Reconstruction Error",
        y_std=std_errors,
    )


def ul_LLE(X, y, random_seed, filename, verbose=False):
    del y, verbose
    data = _as_array(X)
    n_neighbors = min(10, max(2, len(data) - 1))
    component_range = _component_range(
        X,
        require_less_than_features=True,
        require_less_than_neighbors=n_neighbors,
    )
    if not component_range:
        return

    valid_components = []
    reconstruction_error = []
    for n_components in component_range:
        try:
            lle = LocallyLinearEmbedding(
                n_neighbors=n_neighbors,
                n_components=n_components,
                random_state=random_seed,
                n_jobs=-1,
            )
            lle.fit_transform(data)
            valid_components.append(n_components)
            reconstruction_error.append(float(lle.reconstruction_error_))
        except Exception:
            continue

    if not valid_components:
        return

    _plot_line(
        valid_components,
        reconstruction_error,
        "LLE Reconstruction Error",
        "Reconstruction Error",
        f"{filename} LLE Reconstruction Error",
    )

def _resolve_data_path(file_name):
    candidate = Path(file_name)
    search_paths = [
        candidate,
        DATA_DIR / file_name,
        Path.cwd() / file_name,
        Path.cwd() / "Data" / file_name,
    ]
    for path in search_paths:
        if path.exists():
            return path
    raise FileNotFoundError(f"Could not locate dataset '{file_name}'.")


def _image_path(name):
    _ensure_output_dirs()
    return IMAGE_DIR / name


def _param_path(name):
    _ensure_output_dirs()
    return PARAM_DIR / name


def _scaler_for_mode(scalar):
    if scalar == 1:
        return MinMaxScaler()
    if scalar == 2:
        return StandardScaler()
    return None


def _stratify_target(y):
    value_counts = pd.Series(y).value_counts(dropna=False)
    if value_counts.empty or value_counts.min() < 2:
        return None
    return y


def _encode_features(X):
    return pd.get_dummies(X, drop_first=False)


def plot_class_distribution(df, class_col, file_name, X):
    counts = df[class_col].value_counts().sort_index()
    values = counts.values / float(len(df.index)) * 100.0

    fig, ax = plt.subplots()
    bars = ax.bar(range(len(values)), values, edgecolor="black", color="steelblue")
    ax.set_xticks(range(len(values)))
    ax.set_xticklabels([str(label) for label in counts.index], fontsize=12)
    ax.set_xlabel("Class", fontsize=14)
    ax.set_ylabel("Occurrences (% of total)", fontsize=14)
    ax.set_title(f"Class Distribution of {file_name} Dataset", fontsize=14)
    for bar, value in zip(bars, values):
        ax.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width() / 2.0, value, f"{value:.1f}", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=10)
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(_image_path(f"{file_name}-ClassDist.png"))
    plt.close(fig)
    return {label: round(count / df.shape[0], 4) for label, count in counts.items()}


def data_load_no_split(file_name, classifier_col, debug=False, scalar=1, make_graphs=False):
    data_path = _resolve_data_path(file_name)
    df = pd.read_csv(data_path)

    if debug:
        print("Rows:", df.shape[0])
        print("Columns:", df.shape[1])

    y = df[classifier_col].copy()
    X = df.drop(columns=[classifier_col])

    if make_graphs:
        plot_class_distribution(df, classifier_col, Path(file_name).stem, X)

    X_encoded = _encode_features(X)
    scaler = _scaler_for_mode(scalar)
    if scaler is None:
        return X_encoded.copy(), y
    X_scaled = pd.DataFrame(
        scaler.fit_transform(X_encoded),
        index=X_encoded.index,
        columns=X_encoded.columns,
    )
    return X_scaled, y


def data_load(file_name, classifier_col, debug=False, scalar=1, make_graphs=False, random_seed=1):
    data_path = _resolve_data_path(file_name)
    df = pd.read_csv(data_path)

    if debug:
        print("Rows:", df.shape[0])
        print("Columns:", df.shape[1])

    X = df.drop(columns=[classifier_col])

    if make_graphs:
        plot_class_distribution(df, classifier_col, Path(file_name).stem, X)

    X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(

        stratify=_stratify_target(y),

    if scaler is not None:

def heatmap(data, row_labels, col_labels, ax=None, cbar_kw={}, cbarlabel="", **kwargs):
    """
    Create a heatmap from a numpy array and two lists of labels.

    Parameters
    ----------
    data
        A 2D numpy array of shape (N, M).
    row_labels
        A list or array of length N with the labels for the rows.
    col_labels
        A list or array of length M with the labels for the columns.
    ax
        A `matplotlib.axes.Axes` instance to which the heatmap is plotted.  If
        not provided, use current axes or create a new one.  Optional.
    cbar_kw
        A dictionary with arguments to `matplotlib.Figure.colorbar`.  Optional.
    cbarlabel
        The label for the colorbar.  Optional.
    **kwargs
        All other arguments are forwarded to `imshow`.
    """

    if not ax:
        ax = plt.gca()

    # Plot the heatmap
    im = ax.imshow(data, **kwargs)

    # Create colorbar
    cbar = ax.figure.colorbar(im, ax=ax, **cbar_kw)
    cbar.ax.set_ylabel(cbarlabel, rotation=-90, va="bottom")

    # We want to show all ticks...
    ax.set_xticks(np.arange(data.shape[1]))
    ax.set_yticks(np.arange(data.shape[0]))
    # ... and label them with the respective list entries.
    ax.set_xticklabels(col_labels)
    ax.set_yticklabels(row_labels)

    # Let the horizontal axes labeling appear on top.
    ax.tick_params(top=True, bottom=False,
                   labeltop=True, labelbottom=False)

    # Rotate the tick labels and set their alignment.
    plt.setp(ax.get_xticklabels(), rotation=-30, ha="right",
             rotation_mode="anchor")
    plt.title('epsilon')
    plt.ylabel('gamma')

    # Turn spines off and create white grid.
    for edge, spine in ax.spines.items():
        spine.set_visible(False)

    ax.set_xticks(np.arange(data.shape[1] + 1) - .5, minor=True)
    ax.set_yticks(np.arange(data.shape[0] + 1) - .5, minor=True)
    ax.grid(which="minor", color="w", linestyle='-', linewidth=3)
    ax.tick_params(which="minor", bottom=False, left=False)

    return im, cbar


def annotate_heatmap(im, data=None, valfmt="{x:.2f}", textcolors=["black", "white"], threshold=None, **textkw):
    """
    A function to annotate a heatmap.

    Parameters
    ----------
    im
        The AxesImage to be labeled.
    data
        Data used to annotate.  If None, the image's data is used.  Optional.
    valfmt
        The format of the annotations inside the heatmap.  This should either
        use the string format method, e.g. "$ {x:.2f}", or be a
        `matplotlib.ticker.Formatter`.  Optional.
    textcolors
        A list or array of two color specifications.  The first is used for
        values below a threshold, the second for those above.  Optional.
    threshold
        Value in data units according to which the colors from textcolors are
        applied.  If None (the default) uses the middle of the colormap as
        separation.  Optional.
    **kwargs
        All other arguments are forwarded to each call to `text` used to create
        the text labels.
    """

    if not isinstance(data, (list, np.ndarray)):
        data = im.get_array()

    # Normalize the threshold to the images color range.
    if threshold is not None:
        threshold = im.norm(threshold)
    else:
        threshold = im.norm(data.max()) / 2.

    # Set default alignment to center, but allow it to be
    # overwritten by textkw.
    kw = dict(horizontalalignment="center",
              verticalalignment="center")
    kw.update(textkw)

    # Get the formatter in case a string is supplied
    if isinstance(valfmt, str):
        valfmt = matplotlib.ticker.StrMethodFormatter(valfmt)

    # Loop over the data and create a `Text` for each "pixel".
    # Change the text's color depending on the data.
    texts = []
    for i in range(data.shape[0]):
        for j in range(data.shape[1]):
            kw.update(color=textcolors[int(im.norm(data[i, j]) > threshold)])
            text = im.axes.text(j, i, valfmt(data[i, j], None), **kw)
            texts.append(text)

    return texts

from pathlib import Path
import random

import matplotlib
import mdptoolbox.example
import numpy as np
from hiive.mdptoolbox import mdp
from matplotlib import colors, pyplot as plt


BASE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
IMAGE_DIR = BASE_DIR / "Images"


def _ensure_output_dir():
    IMAGE_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)


def _image_path(name):
    _ensure_output_dir()
    return IMAGE_DIR / name


def heatmap(data, row_labels, col_labels, ax=None, cbar_kw=None, cbarlabel="", **kwargs):
    if ax is None:
        ax = plt.gca()
    if cbar_kw is None:
        cbar_kw = {}

    im = ax.imshow(data, **kwargs)
    cbar = ax.figure.colorbar(im, ax=ax, **cbar_kw)
    cbar.ax.set_ylabel(cbarlabel, rotation=-90, va="bottom")

    ax.set_xticks(np.arange(data.shape[1]))
    ax.set_yticks(np.arange(data.shape[0]))
    ax.set_xticklabels(col_labels)
    ax.set_yticklabels(row_labels)
    ax.tick_params(top=True, bottom=False, labeltop=True, labelbottom=False)
    plt.setp(ax.get_xticklabels(), rotation=-30, ha="right", rotation_mode="anchor")
    ax.set_title("epsilon")
    ax.set_ylabel("gamma")

    for spine in ax.spines.values():
        spine.set_visible(False)

    ax.set_xticks(np.arange(data.shape[1] + 1) - 0.5, minor=True)
    ax.set_yticks(np.arange(data.shape[0] + 1) - 0.5, minor=True)
    ax.grid(which="minor", color="w", linestyle="-", linewidth=3)
    ax.tick_params(which="minor", bottom=False, left=False)
    return im, cbar


def annotate_heatmap(im, data=None, valfmt="{x:.2f}", textcolors=("black", "white"), threshold=None, **textkw):
    if data is None:
        data = im.get_array()
    elif not isinstance(data, np.ndarray):
        data = np.asarray(data)

    if threshold is not None:
        threshold = im.norm(threshold)
    else:
        threshold = im.norm(np.max(data)) / 2.0

    kw = {"horizontalalignment": "center", "verticalalignment": "center"}
    kw.update(textkw)

    if isinstance(valfmt, str):
        valfmt = matplotlib.ticker.StrMethodFormatter(valfmt)

    texts = []
    for i in range(data.shape[0]):
        for j in range(data.shape[1]):
            kw["color"] = textcolors[int(im.norm(data[i, j]) > threshold)]
            texts.append(im.axes.text(j, i, valfmt(data[i, j], None), **kw))
    return texts


def run_episodes(policy, S, R, p, num_episodes, num_resets):
    rewards = []
    for _ in range(num_resets):
        state = 0
        total_reward = 0.0
        for _ in range(num_episodes):
            state = min(state, S - 1)
            if np.random.random() <= p:
                state = 0
                continue

            action = int(policy[state])
            total_reward += float(R[state][action])
            if action == 1:
                state = 0
            else:
                state = min(state + 1, S - 1)
        rewards.append(total_reward)
    return float(np.mean(rewards))


def _plot_run_stats(run_stats, prefix, size):
    if not run_stats:
        return
    iterations = [entry["Iteration"] for entry in run_stats if "Iteration" in entry]
    mean_val = [entry["Mean V"] for entry in run_stats if "Mean V" in entry]
    error = [entry["Error"] for entry in run_stats if "Error" in entry]
    reward = [entry["Reward"] for entry in run_stats if "Reward" in entry]
    if not iterations:
        return

    fig, ax = plt.subplots()
    if mean_val:
        ax.plot(iterations[: len(mean_val)], mean_val, label="Mean V")
    if error:
        ax.plot(iterations[: len(error)], error, label="Error")
    if reward:
        ax.plot(iterations[: len(reward)], reward, label="Reward")
    ax.legend()
    ax.set_xlabel("Iterations", fontsize=15)
    ax.set_ylabel("V / Error / Reward", fontsize=15)
    ax.set_title("Mean V / Error / Reward vs Iterations")
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(_image_path(f"{prefix}-Forest-RunStats-{size}.png"))
    plt.close(fig)


def _plot_heatmap(data, gammas, epsilons, title, label, filename, formatter):
    fig, ax = plt.subplots()
    im, _ = heatmap(data, gammas, epsilons, ax=ax, cmap="YlGn", cbarlabel=label)
    annotate_heatmap(im, valfmt=formatter)
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(_image_path(filename))
    plt.close(fig)


def _plot_policy(best_policy_by_gamma, gammas, size, prefix):
    if not best_policy_by_gamma:
        return
    policy_matrix = np.asarray(best_policy_by_gamma, dtype=int)
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 3.75))
    cmap = colors.ListedColormap(["blue", "red"])
    ax.pcolor(policy_matrix[::-1], cmap=cmap, edgecolors="k", linewidths=0)
    ax.set_title(f"Forest {prefix} Policy - Red = Cut, Blue = Wait")
    ax.set_xlabel("State", fontsize=15)
    ax.set_ylabel("Gamma", fontsize=15)
    ax.set_yticks(np.arange(0.5, len(gammas) + 0.5, 1.0))
    ax.set_yticklabels(list(reversed(gammas)), fontsize=12)
    ax.tick_params(left=False)
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(_image_path(f"{prefix}-Forest-Heatmap-{size}.png"))
    plt.close(fig)


def run_forest(size):
    seed_val = 42
    np.random.seed(seed_val)
    random.seed(seed_val)

    S = size
    r1 = 10
    r2 = 50
    p = 0.1
    P, R = mdptoolbox.example.forest(S=S, r1=r1, r2=r2, p=p)

    gammas = [0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9, 0.99]
    epsilons = [0.1, 0.01, 0.001, 0.0001]

    reward_hm = np.zeros((len(gammas), len(epsilons)))
    iter_hm = np.zeros((len(gammas), len(epsilons)))
    time_hm = np.zeros((len(gammas), len(epsilons)))

    best_reward = float("-inf")
    best_run_stats = None
    best_policy_by_gamma = []

    for g_idx, gamma in enumerate(gammas):
        gamma_best_reward = float("-inf")
        gamma_best_policy = np.zeros(S, dtype=int)
        for e_idx, epsilon in enumerate(epsilons):
            solver = mdp.ValueIteration(P, R, gamma=gamma, epsilon=epsilon)
            solver.run()
            reward = run_episodes(solver.policy, S, R, p, num_episodes=1000, num_resets=20)

            reward_hm[g_idx, e_idx] = reward
            iter_hm[g_idx, e_idx] = float(solver.iter)
            time_hm[g_idx, e_idx] = float(solver.time * 1000.0)

            if reward > gamma_best_reward:
                gamma_best_reward = reward
                gamma_best_policy = np.asarray(solver.policy, dtype=int)
            if reward > best_reward:
                best_reward = reward
                best_run_stats = list(solver.run_stats) if solver.run_stats is not None else None

        best_policy_by_gamma.append(gamma_best_policy.tolist())

    _plot_run_stats(best_run_stats, "VI", size)
    _plot_heatmap(
        reward_hm,
        gammas,
        epsilons,
        "Average Reward",
        "Average Reward",
        f"VI-Forest-Per_Heatmap-{size}.png",
        "{x:.0f}",
    )
    _plot_heatmap(
        iter_hm,
        gammas,
        epsilons,
        "Iterations to Convergence",
        "# of Iterations to Convergence",
        f"VI-Forest-Iter_Heatmap-{size}.png",
        "{x:.0f}",
    )
    _plot_heatmap(
        time_hm,
        gammas,
        epsilons,
        "Runtime (ms)",
        "Runtime (ms)",
        f"VI-Forest-Time_Heatmap-{size}.png",
        "{x:.1f}",
    )
    _plot_policy(best_policy_by_gamma, gammas, size, "VI")

    return {
        "gammas": gammas,
        "epsilons": epsilons,
        "reward_heatmap": reward_hm,
        "iteration_heatmap": iter_hm,
        "time_heatmap": time_hm,
        "best_reward": best_reward,
        "policies": best_policy_by_gamma,
    }


if __name__ == "__main__":
    run_forest(10)
    run_forest(1000)

def heatmap(data, row_labels, col_labels, ax=None, cbar_kw={}, cbarlabel="", **kwargs):
    """
    Create a heatmap from a numpy array and two lists of labels.

    Parameters
    ----------
    data
        A 2D numpy array of shape (N, M).

        A list or array of length N with the labels for the rows.

    if not ax:

    cbar.ax.set_ylabel(cbarlabel, rotation=-90, va="bottom")

    # We want to show all ticks...
    ax.set_xticks(np.arange(data.shape[1]))
    ax.set_yticks(np.arange(data.shape[0]))
    # ... and label them with the respective list entries.
    ax.set_xticklabels(col_labels)
    ax.set_yticklabels(row_labels)

    # Let the horizontal axes labeling appear on top.
    ax.tick_params(top=True, bottom=False,
                   labeltop=True, labelbottom=False)

    ax.set_yticks(np.arange(data.shape[0] + 1) - .5, minor=True)

    return im, cbar


def annotate_heatmap(im, data=None, valfmt="{x:.2f}", textcolors=["black", "white"], threshold=None, **textkw):
    """
    A function to annotate a heatmap.

    Parameters
    ----------
    im
        The AxesImage to be labeled.
    data
        Data used to annotate.  If None, the image's data is used.  Optional.
    valfmt
        The format of the annotations inside the heatmap.  This should either
        use the string format method, e.g. "$ {x:.2f}", or be a
        `matplotlib.ticker.Formatter`.  Optional.
    textcolors
        A list or array of two color specifications.  The first is used for
        values below a threshold, the second for those above.  Optional.
    threshold
        Value in data units according to which the colors from textcolors are
        applied.  If None (the default) uses the middle of the colormap as
        separation.  Optional.
    **kwargs
        All other arguments are forwarded to each call to `text` used to create
        the text labels.
    """

    if not isinstance(data, (list, np.ndarray)):
        data = im.get_array()

    # Normalize the threshold to the images color range.
    if threshold is not None:
        threshold = im.norm(threshold)
    else:
        threshold = im.norm(data.max()) / 2.

    # Set default alignment to center, but allow it to be
    # overwritten by textkw.
    kw = dict(horizontalalignment="center",
              verticalalignment="center")
    kw.update(textkw)

    # Get the formatter in case a string is supplied
    if isinstance(valfmt, str):
        valfmt = matplotlib.ticker.StrMethodFormatter(valfmt)

    # Loop over the data and create a `Text` for each "pixel".
    # Change the text's color depending on the data.
    texts = []
    for i in range(data.shape[0]):
        for j in range(data.shape[1]):
            kw.update(color=textcolors[int(im.norm(data[i, j]) > threshold)])
            text = im.axes.text(j, i, valfmt(data[i, j], None), **kw)
            texts.append(text)

    data
        Data used to annotate.  If None, the image's data is used.  Optional.
    valfmt
        The format of the annotations inside the heatmap.  This should either
        use the string format method, e.g. "$ {x:.2f}", or be a
        `matplotlib.ticker.Formatter`.  Optional.
    textcolors
        A list or array of two color specifications.  The first is used for
        values below a threshold, the second for those above.  Optional.
    threshold
        Value in data units according to which the colors from textcolors are
        applied.  If None (the default) uses the middle of the colormap as
        separation.  Optional.
    **kwargs
        All other arguments are forwarded to each call to `text` used to create
        the text labels.
    """

    if not isinstance(data, (list, np.ndarray)):
        data = im.get_array()

    # Normalize the threshold to the images color range.
    if threshold is not None:
        threshold = im.norm(threshold)
    else:
        threshold = im.norm(data.max()) / 2.

    # Set default alignment to center, but allow it to be
    # overwritten by textkw.
    kw = dict(horizontalalignment="center",
              verticalalignment="center")
    kw.update(textkw)

    # Get the formatter in case a string is supplied
    if isinstance(valfmt, str):
        valfmt = matplotlib.ticker.StrMethodFormatter(valfmt)

    # Loop over the data and create a `Text` for each "pixel".
    # Change the text's color depending on the data.
    texts = []
    for i in range(data.shape[0]):
        for j in range(data.shape[1]):
            kw.update(color=textcolors[int(im.norm(data[i, j]) > threshold)])
            text = im.axes.text(j, i, valfmt(data[i, j], None), **kw)
            texts.append(text)

    return texts


# Citation: https://learning.oreilly.com/library/view/reinforcement-learning-algorithms/9781789131116/ab06aa68-01f9-481e-94ac-4c6748c3b858.xhtml
def eval_state_action(env, V, s, a, gamma=0.99):
    return np.sum([p * ((rew - 0.01 * _) + gamma * V[next_s]) for p, next_s, rew, _ in env.P[s][a]])


def policy_evaluation(env, V, policy, nS, epsilon=0.0001, gamma=0.99):
    while True:
        delta = 0
        for s in range(nS):
            old_v = V[s]
            V[s] = eval_state_action(env, V, s, policy[s], gamma)
            delta = max(delta, np.abs(old_v - V[s]))
        if delta < epsilon:
            break


def policy_improvement(env, V, policy, nA, nS, gamma=0.99):
    policy_stable = True
    for s in range(nS):
        old_a = policy[s]
        policy[s] = np.argmax([eval_state_action(env, V, s, a, gamma) for a in range(nA)])
        if old_a != policy[s]:
            policy_stable = False
    return policy_stable


def run_pi_episodes(env, V, policy, num_games=100):
    tot_rew = 0
    state = env.reset()
    for _ in range(num_games):
        done = False
        tot_run = 0
        while not done:
            next_state, reward, done, _ = env.step(policy[state])
            state = next_state
            tot_rew += reward
            tot_run += 1
            if done or tot_run > 1000:
                done = True
                state = env.reset()
    return float(tot_rew / num_games)

def _param_grid(classifier, full_param):
    prefix = "estimator" if "estimator" in classifier.get_params() else "base_estimator"
    return [
        {
            f"{prefix}__criterion": ["gini", "entropy"],
            f"{prefix}__max_depth": [1, 2, 3, 5, 10] if full_param else [1, 2, 3, 5],

            "random_state": [1],
        }
    ]


def train_BTree(
    filename,
    X_train,
    X_test,
    y_train,
    y_test,
    full_param=False,
    debug=False,
    numFolds=10,
    njobs=-1,
    scalar=1,
    make_graphs=False,
    pBTree={},
):
    start = time.time()
    algo = "BoostedTree"
    file_stem = Path(str(filename)).stem
    params = util.normalize_adaboost_params(pBTree)

    if params:
        classifier = util.create_adaboost_classifier(
            estimator=DecisionTreeClassifier(random_state=params.get("random_state", 1)),
            random_state=params.get("random_state", 1),
        )
        classifier.set_params(**params)
    else:
        classifier = util.create_adaboost_classifier(
            estimator=DecisionTreeClassifier(random_state=1),
            random_state=1,
        )
        grid_search = GridSearchCV(
            classifier,
            param_grid=_param_grid(classifier, full_param),
            cv=min(numFolds, util._safe_cv_folds(y_train, numFolds)),
            scoring=util.get_roc_auc_scorer(y_train),
            return_train_score=True,
            n_jobs=njobs,
            verbose=int(bool(debug)),
        )
        grid_search.fit(X_train, y_train)
        util.save_gridsearch_to_csv(grid_search.cv_results_, algo, file_stem, scalar)
        classifier = grid_search.best_estimator_
        params = classifier.get_params()

    classifier.fit(X_train, y_train)
    train_score = util.score_estimator(classifier, X_train, y_train)
    test_score = util.score_estimator(classifier, X_test, y_test)

    if make_graphs:
        util.plot_learning_curve(
            classifier,
            algo,
            file_stem,
            X_train,
            y_train,
            ylim=(0.0, 1.05),
            cv=min(numFolds, util._safe_cv_folds(y_train, numFolds)),
            n_jobs=njobs,
            debug=debug,
        )
        util.boost_lr_vs_nest(X_train, y_train, params, njobs, file_stem, test_score)

        prefix = "estimator" if "estimator" in classifier.get_params() else "base_estimator"
        for parameter, values, options in [
            ("n_estimators", [25, 50, 100, 200, 300], {}),
            ("learning_rate", [0.01, 0.1, 0.5, 1.0], {"log": True}),
            (f"{prefix}__max_depth", [1, 2, 3, 5, 10], {}),
            (f"{prefix}__criterion", ["gini", "entropy"], {"fString": True}),
        ]:
            base_params = dict(params)
            base_params.pop(parameter, None)
            test_class = util.create_adaboost_classifier(
                estimator=DecisionTreeClassifier(random_state=base_params.get("random_state", 1)),
                random_state=base_params.get("random_state", 1),
            )
            test_class.set_params(**base_params)
            util.compute_vc(
                algo,
                parameter,
                values,
                X_train,
                y_train,
                X_test,
                y_test,
                classifier,
                file_stem,
                test_class,
                base_params,
                njobs=njobs,
                debug=debug,
                **options,
            )

    return time.time() - start, float(train_score), float(test_score)
